learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to represent algorithms independently of programming languages.
They can independently create small programs using the C programming language.
They are able to understand and further develop given C programs.
Students know the basic elements of imperative programming and can apply them in programming.
Students are able to structure and modularize C programs using functions.
Students know and use the standard basic data types (int, float, char) of the C programming language.
They are also able to declare, define, and use composite data types.
Students are able to independently program simple mathematical functions and calculations and evaluate the results of their programs.

syllabus_topics: Formal foundations of computer science (set theory, Boolean algebra, propositional logic, Turing machine, von Neumann architecture, number systems, 2's complement)
The C programming language and its standard libraries
Abstract data type as a summary of data and operations
Basic data types, composite data types in the C programming language
Control structures (blocks, conditional statements, loops, functions)
assessment_rules: To receive credit points, the module examination must be passed and proof of achievement must be provided. The grading conforms to the study and examination regulations (SPO).
